Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with `README.md`, then inspect the current rollout artifacts and both required wake views before touching the policy. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf now, since this is the first architecture proposal from the common seed.

The workspace is a single-candidate policy task; CFD is explicitly out of scope. I’m now reading the inherited control lessons, the bookshelf transfer rules and references, and inventorying all sampled rollout evidence so the diagnosis is tied to what actually happened.

All four samples are valid direct-uniform still-water captures, not failures; their separation is terminal quality and arrival time. I’m inspecting every combined sheet now—especially the best-score `23.4245T` pair versus the slower `23.8645T` sample—then I’ll quantify the policy and trajectory differences rather than infer them from score alone.

The top-down sheets show the same self-propelled route and coherent alternating mid-plane street through capture. The oblique rows are blank render artifacts in these sampled sheets, so I won’t claim independent 3D structure from them; I’m checking the separate oblique files and manifest, then using trajectory/load diagnostics to distinguish the candidates.

The sampled policies isolate two real effects: water-relative axial recovery improves the no-reflex baseline from `23.8645T` to `23.4245T`, while adverse-moment rejection improves the inertial-speed branch to `23.5455T`. The untested, evidence-supported candidate is their small compatible combination. Before formalizing it, I’m completing the required bookshelf transfer on load-aware steering and locomotor-relative sensing.

The bookshelf reinforces exactly one compact transfer: keep target geometry as the slow route command and use a soft, dead-banded normalized moment residual only for adverse hydrodynamic yaw. I’m now checking its sign, activation, and envelope against the best trace so the combination is not merely “add two winners.”

The residual is genuinely bounded on the best trace (offline maximum `2.70°`, mean `0.38°`) and acts on adverse moments while preserving the carrier; its standalone branch also reduced mean action and peak load versus the inertial no-reflex baseline. I’m recording the pre-edit diagnosis and falsification contract now, before changing the candidate as required.

The candidate now makes one semantic change to the assigned parent: the anterior recovery gate measures through-water axial speed, while the independently positive adverse-moment residual is retained unchanged. I’m updating the durable experience bank with the newest matched evidence and its limits, then I’ll run the policy contract checks.

The durable guidance now records the new positive observation-frame result and the bounded load-allocation result, including their untested compatibility and visual-evidence boundary. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated check runner now; it will validate the policy and guidance without running CFD.

The dedicated checker could not start because its configured model is unavailable in this runtime. I’m falling back to the checker’s own local instructions and will run the same deterministic validations directly; no CFD will be launched.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same prefill guidance parent twice, so the checker sees two copied parents before comparing any content. I’m inspecting that guard now and will make the smallest workspace-metadata repair needed for an unambiguous assigned parent, then rerun it.

The guidance guard and Julia policy contract now pass; the candidate returns finite two-joint acceleration and its parameter schema resolves correctly. I’m running the final boundary check to confirm no forbidden solver files changed.

All three prescribed checks pass. I’m doing a final audit of the exact candidate delta and required artifacts now; no CFD has been run, so the combined mechanism remains a falsifiable rollout candidate rather than a claimed improvement.

Produced exactly one candidate combining water-relative locomotor recovery with the assigned parent’s bounded adverse-moment rejection.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:185)

The rendered README’s duplicate parent marker was removed so the required guidance checker could resolve one assigned parent.

All prescribed non-CFD checks passed: guidance materiality, finite two-joint Julia contract/schema, and solver boundary. The configured checker agent itself was unavailable due its unsupported model, so its three commands were run directly. No CFD evaluation was performed.
